short: Closed-loop formant decoding (M06), F1/F2 output (M08) and wireless telemetry (M13) are standard: vowels learnable in one user; hit rate lacks a chance level; no speech measured.
position: The paper [@guenther2009] changed the decoder into a closed loop (M06, Kalman filter to formants, audio 30–70 ms after neural firing), the output into two formants of a Klatt synthesizer (M08) and the link into transcutaneous telemetry (M13). All three are standard under our rules: the ledger holds no earlier closed loop from a non-acoustic signal (Appendix), but one participant with one electrode gives no repetition. The main claim, that a locked-in user learns to steer synthesized vowels, holds. Its measure is weak: the 45% to 70% hit rate between the opening and closing blocks (Discussion) is helped by an attractor force in the target regions and has no chance level or decoder-off control (Methods). Nothing measures speech, so "near-conversational synthetic speech output" (Abstract) is a projection; this is the protocol ancestor of the [later] sentence closed loop at 43.75% WER [@wairagkar2025], not a performance reference.
